detect.title: Detecting features
detect.intro: Connecting to your device and watching which values change. This takes about half a minute.
detect.failed: Could not read from your device
detect.no_data: Something answers at this address, but it returns no NIBE data. Check the IP is your device's own and that Modbus TCP is on (menu 7.5.9).

features.title: Select features
features.intro: Choose which features to monitor. Recommendations are based on what your device reported.
features.insights_note: Disabling a feature removes its capabilities, including their Insights history.

discover.searching: Searching your network for Nibe heat pumps…
discover.none_found: No heat pump found automatically. Check that Modbus TCP is enabled on your device (menu 7.5.9) or enter its IP address below.
discover.title: Find your heat pump
discover.confirm: Found your heat pump — tap to confirm

devices.title: Add devices
devices.intro: Each function of your device becomes its own device in Homey. The ones we found live data for are checked, but you can add any of them.
devices.select_one: Select at least one device to add.
devices.main_desc: Overview: outdoor temperature, operating priority and mode, plus diagnostics and statistics
devices.analytics_desc: Helps the app author see which models and features are actually used, and where setup fails. No personal data, no readings from your home, no network details. You can change this later under app settings.

sources.prompt: More than one sensor can report this. Pick the one that should regulate:

tank.title: Hot water tank
tank.hint: Needed for the hot water estimate. One entry per family — the lining doesn't matter.
tank.inlet_hint: 10 °C is the usual figure; a little lower in winter, higher in summer.

setup.title: Device Setup
setup.intro: Set up the functions you selected.
setup.heating_intro: Choose the temperature that guides your heating.
setup.nibe: Use your device’s own temperature sensor
setup.homey: Use your own Homey temperature sensors
setup.promise: Let your rooms guide the heating
setup.promise_desc: Use the temperature sensors you already have in Homey. Choose one room, or average several for a temperature that represents your home. Your device keeps its thermostat and Smart Price Adaption.
setup.picker_intro: Find sensors by name, room, device type or app. Choose one or combine several.
setup.review_intro: Each selected sensor has equal influence.
setup.pending_hint: Add your devices first, then open Heating → Repair to finish the setup. Leave your current NIBE sensor in control until then. No temperatures are sent during pairing.
setup.pump_intro: Check these settings on your device, then verify here.
setup.pump_enable: Enable external room sensor BT50 in menu 7.5.9.2.
setup.pump_zone: Assign BT50 to your heating zone in room sensor / zone settings (1.3.3 / 1.3.4).
setup.pump_control: Select BT50 to control heating. Remove the previous controlling sensor if you want to replace it.
setup.zone_confirm: I have selected BT50 to control the intended zone.
setup.feed_warning: Verify settings starts regular temperature updates. They continue when you close Repair. If Homey or a selected sensor stops supplying valid readings, BT50 can alarm; restore your NIBE sensor and disable external BT50 on your device. Complete this step while you can access your device.
setup.verified: Your device received the temperature at BT50.
setup.active_note: Temperature updates continue in the background. To stop them, use Heating Setup to return to your NIBE sensor first.
setup.handover_hint: On your device, select your original sensor to control the zone and disable external BT50. The current feed continues until you verify here.
setup.handover_confirm: My NIBE sensor is controlling the zone again.
setup.no_nibe_sources: No live NIBE source choices were detected. The current/default source will be kept.
setup.thermostat_zone_title: Which zone should the thermostat set?
setup.thermostat_zone_intro: Your device has more than one zone. Choose the zone that controls the heating: on your device, that zone’s room sensor is set to control (menu 1.3.3).
setup.analytics_benefit: Nibe Live is built by one developer with one heat pump. Sharing how the app works with yours helps uncover compatibility issues, improve setup and focus development on the features you use.
setup.analytics_details: Includes your device model, app features used and technical events such as setup failures and connection problems. Temperature readings, device names and Flow names are never included.
setup.analytics_optional: Optional. Turn it off anytime in device settings → Privacy.
setup.request_timeout: Homey did not respond. Please try again.
setup.source_intro: Choose which sensor supplies the indoor temperature used to control your heating.
setup.source_homey_desc: Use one sensor or average several rooms. Your device stays in control.
setup.feed_short: Verification starts regular temperature updates, which continue after you close Repair.
setup.feed_recovery: If Homey or a sensor stops reporting, BT50 may alarm. Restore the NIBE sensor and disable external BT50 on your device.
setup.zone_detail: Menus 1.3.3 / 1.3.4 · Assign BT50 to the zone you want to heat.
setup.control_detail: Replace the previous controlling sensor if needed.
setup.success_description: Your device is now receiving temperatures from your Homey sensors.

smart.title: Smart mode
smart.section_heating: Who moves heating to cheaper hours.
smart.section_hotwater: Who moves hot water to cheaper hours.
smart.intro: Pick one. Only one can steer the compressor.
smart.choose_on_desc_heating: Runs in Nibe Live and learns your house.
smart.choose_on_desc_hotwater: Runs in Nibe Live and learns how you use hot water.
smart.choose_spa_desc: NIBE's own, runs in your device.
smart.choose_off_desc_hotwater: Hot water follows your device's own settings.
smart.success_description: Comfort range, Away and status are on the Heating device. The thermostat sets the comfort temperature.
smart.choose_test_desc: Shows what it would do. Changes nothing.
smart.spa_note: Autopilot turns off Smart price adaption for heating.
smart.indoor_missing: Set up the indoor temperature under Heating first.
smart.outdoor_forecast: Weather forecast. A sensor in the shade is more accurate.
smart.prices_fixed: Fixed price: nothing to shift. Set dynamic prices in Homey Energy.
smart.room_control_on: On in your device. Turn it off: your device would correct by room temperature and undo the shifts Autopilot makes.
smart.room_control_unknown: Could not be read. Keep it off.
smart.bt1_detail: Menu 7.5.9.2 on your device: turn on external BT1.
smart.verify_intro: Autopilot checks that your device takes its outdoor temperature.
smart.return_reminder: On your device, turn off external BT1 in menu 7.5.9.2.
smart.outdoor_intro: Pick a sensor in the shade, or use the forecast.
smart.steer_intro: Pick one. Only one can steer the compressor.
smart.pump_intro: What your device needs for your choices.
smart.room_control_optional: Optional. On lets your device correct by room temperature. Turn it off before choosing Autopilot.
smart.pump_confirm: These are set on your device
smart.row_cheaper: Heats more when power is cheap, less when it's expensive
smart.row_learns: Learns how your house holds heat
smart.cmp_note: Smart price adaption is NIBE's own: it runs in your device and gets prices through myUplink.
smart.exp_learning_sub: At least 5 days. Nothing changes yet.
smart.exp_acting_sub: Heat moves around price peaks, within your Comfort range.
smart.ctl_away_sub: A lower temperature while you're out
smart.section_pool: Who moves pool heating to cheaper hours.
smart.section_cooling: Who moves cooling to cheaper hours.
smart.choose_on_desc_pool: Will heat the pool in cheap and solar hours, within a band you set.
smart.choose_on_desc_cooling: Will pre-cool before price peaks and on solar surplus.
smart.choose_off_desc_pool: The pool follows your device's own settings.
smart.choose_off_desc_cooling: Cooling follows your device's own settings.
smart.hw_intro: Two things before Autopilot takes over hot water.
smart.hw_flows: Flows that switch More hot water
smart.hw_flows_none: None. Only Autopilot will start charges.
smart.hw_flows_found: These start charges Autopilot did not plan. Turn them off, or keep them for notifications only:
smart.hw_flows_unknown: Your Flows could not be read. Turn off any that switch More hot water on a schedule.
smart.hw_household_intro: Your device has __days__ days of hot water history. Until it has two weeks, Autopilot also starts from these answers.
smart.hw_household_intro_unknown: Until your device has two weeks of hot water history, Autopilot starts from these answers.
smart.hw_morning: Morning shower on a working day
smart.hw_free: On a day off, most hot water is used
smart.household_invalid: Choose how many people live there and a shower time.
smart.solar_intro: Autopilot can heat with your own solar power.
smart.solar_scanning: Looking for energy meters in your home…
smart.solar_meter_pick: Several found. Pick the one for your whole home.
smart.solar_evidence: In recent weeks you sent up to __kw__ kW to the grid on sunny hours.
smart.solar_evidence_plain: Your meter sends power to the grid on sunny hours.
smart.solar_live_hint: Hot water charges while your home exports power.
smart.solar_forecast_hint: Can skip a night charge when sun is forecast. Leave off if a battery or car charger uses your solar first.
smart.solar_no_meter_found: Found your solar panels, but no electricity meter that measures what you sell, like a P1 reader. Add it to Homey Energy, then come back here.
smart.solar_need_meter: Solar heating needs an electricity meter that measures what you sell, like a P1 reader. Add it to Homey Energy, then come back here.

gateway.title: Gateway connection
gateway.hint: Choose how NIBE register 40025 is addressed on your connection. Confirm with a working Modbus query. The same convention applies to all reads and writes.
gateway.invalid: Choose a gateway, a port from 1–65535 and a Modbus ID from 1–247.
gateway.detect_intro: Checking the values your device reports. Depending on the gateway, this can take several minutes.

firmware.title: Update your device first
firmware.intro: Many features need recent software on your device. Older versions miss readings the app relies on and can even report wrong energy figures.
firmware.online_body: When an update is waiting, approve it in the myUplink app — or on your device's display: swipe to the product overview and tap Update.
firmware.usb_body: Download the latest software from myuplink.com and put it on a USB stick. Insert it in the port above the display and open menu 8.1.
firmware.f_title: Via myUplink or a USB stick
firmware.f_body: The steps differ between models — your device's manual shows how.
firmware.note: Takes a few minutes. Your settings are kept.

connection.searching: Can't reach your device at __host__. Searching the network for it…

connection.address_in_use: Another paired heat pump already uses __host__.
